title: RAG: look it up before answering
subtitle: Giving the model an honest cheat sheet
mission: Make the Sunflower School assistant answer front-office questions using the school’s documents. Then turn search off and see what happens.

predict.question: guess: a model has never read Sunflower School’s documents. With no search, you ask when the July break ends. It…

options.invents: Gives a date, full of confidence
options.knows: Gets it right, models know everything

feedback.right: yes, and that’s why this step exists. But first the good side: with search on, the answer comes from the Calendar, with the source cited.
feedback.wrong: close. Models tend to answer confidently even when they don’t know. Notice: with search on, the answer comes from the Calendar, with the source cited.

why.simples:
The model is like a student who has read loads, but never saw your school’s notebook. If you just ask, it guesses. RAG means letting it open the right notebook before answering, and say which page the answer came from.
If the answer isn’t in the notebook, the right thing is to say “I couldn’t find it”.
why.dev:
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) has three stages: 1) retrieve the chunks most similar to the question, usually with embeddings (step 5); 2) paste those chunks into the prompt; 3) ask the model to answer only from them and cite the source.
Here retrieval is by shared words (easier to see); the relevance threshold decides whether a chunk is good enough or the answer is “not found”.
why.especialista:
RAG quality is, first of all, retrieval quality: chunk size, hybrid search (vector + keyword), reranking, and metadata such as date and permissions.
Measure retrieval (did the right chunk come back?) and generation (is the answer grounded in it?) separately. Stale documents produce wrong answers with sources: RAG cites the error confidently. And every pasted chunk is untrusted input (prompt injection comes in the Production track).

mission.ui: time to break it. Turn search off and ask again when the July break ends.
mission.cmd: time to break it. Run the same question with --search no.

break.success: Broken: without the documents, the model invented a convincing, sourceless answer. That’s hallucination: the text sounds right, but rests on nothing.
break.calm: With search on it held on to the documents. To break it, turn search off.

ui: Pick one of the ready-made questions and hit Run.
“Chunks” is how many document pieces get pasted into the request.
To see hallucination: turn “Search the documents” off and run.
cmd: The question goes in quotes, after ask.
--search yes or no turns document lookup on and off.
ask "When does the July break end?" --search no

errors.notBool.search: --search takes yes or no. Example: --search no
errors.aboveMax.top: Up to 4 chunks: the school only has 4 documents. In real life, pasting too much also hurts (and costs tokens).
errors.belowMin.top: At least 1 chunk, or search is pointless.
errors.notInteger.top: Chunks is a whole number, like --chunks 2.

docs.title: 2026 Calendar
docs.text: The July break runs from July 13 to 24. Classes resume on July 27. The parents’ meeting is on August 8.
docs.answer: The July break runs from July 13 to 24, and classes resume on the 27th.
docs.wrong: The July break starts on the 1st and lasts until the end of the month.

docs.title: Uniform
docs.text: The uniform is a yellow T-shirt with the embroidered sunflower and navy trousers or shorts. On Fridays, any T-shirt is fine.
docs.answer: A yellow T-shirt with the embroidered sunflower and navy trousers or shorts. Any T-shirt on Fridays.
docs.wrong: The uniform is a white T-shirt and jeans.

docs.title: Canteen
docs.text: The canteen opens from 9:30 to 15:00. It takes Pix and cards; no cash.
docs.answer: No. The canteen only takes Pix and cards, from 9:30 to 15:00.
docs.wrong: Yes, the canteen takes cash, Pix and cards.

docs.title: Leaving and lateness
docs.text: Up to 15 minutes late: the student joins the first class. Leaving early only with a note signed by a guardian.
docs.answer: Leaving early only with a note signed by a guardian. Up to 15 minutes late still joins the first class.
docs.wrong: You can leave early, just tell the teacher.

steps: In an AI chat, ask: “When does the July break end at my school?”. Notice whether it guesses or asks which school.
Now paste your school’s real calendar (or a piece of it) and write: “Answer only from this text and say where you got it. If it isn’t in the text, say you couldn’t find it”.
Ask again, then ask something that isn’t in the text.
recipe.ok: with the text pasted, the answer uses its dates and cites the passage; for what isn’t in the text, it says it couldn’t find it.
